About AI discoveries in 2024

This selection contains 593 catalog entries dated 2 Jan 2024 to 31 Dec 2024. 593 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

31 Dec 2024Fudan University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

Neural-network interpretation identifies a metabolic panel associated with Moyamoya disease

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A neural network learned serum patterns distinguishing Moyamoya disease from healthy controls. Model interpretation helped select six metabolic signals; their later three-center evaluation reported AUC 0.867, rather than the higher full-fingerprint result.

Technology: Neural network; integrated gradients

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The network learns diagnostic patterns; integrated gradients guides signal selection alongside statistical comparisons.
Test and result
Discovery data comprised 144 patients and 144 controls; repeated spectra were averaged per sample. The six-signal panel was evaluated in 86 later samples, including 49 cases.
Limitation / still unknown
Selected case-control evaluation; preprocessing and feature-selection nesting are incompletely established. Metabolite assignments are tentative. No population screening, stroke prevention or mechanistic claim.

30 Dec 2024ATLAS Collaboration; CERN Large Hadron Collider

OmniFold enables an unbinned 24-dimensional Z+jets cross-section measurement by ATLAS

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset. The measured total fiducial cross section is 1,808 ± 42 fb; most illustrative differential bins have 3–5% total uncertainty, rising to about 15% in tails. The measurement is more precise than the compared predictions for many distributions, especially Sherpa. The event-level release also supports derived observables, including an infrared-and-collinear-safe τ₂₁ measurement in a specified fiducial region.

Technology: OmniFold iterative machine-learning unfolding

Editorial relevance 60 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
OmniFold used neural-network classifiers to iteratively reweight simulated events so the detector-level simulation matched collision data, then propagated the learned correction to particle-level events. That multivariate unfolding handled 24 correlated observables simultaneously and produced event weights with uncertainty variations, enabling a high-dimensional unbinned measurement and event-level construction of additional derived observables. The paper validates closure on pseudo-data and reports its uncertainty components.
Test and result
Using 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton data, ATLAS simultaneously unfolded 24 correlated Z+jets kinematic observables with the machine-learning method OmniFold and released the particle-level result as an unbinned event dataset.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a new high-dimensional precision measurement of known Z+jets production, not a new particle or beyond-Standard-Model discovery. The released measurement is unbinned in 24 measured variables; displayed plots may be binned for presentation. The authors report mostly 3–5% uncertainties in illustrative bins, up to about 15% in tails, with dominant unfolding-prior/hidden-variable uncertainties for some observables. Pseudo-data closure is generally good, with exceptions including a p-value of 0.038 for leading-jet transverse momentum; users are given phase-space and covariance-use guidance.

30 Dec 2024Institute for Artificial Intelligence & Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

Machine-learning screening identifies two drug-repurposing candidates against tuberculosis

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A virtual-screening workflow combined XGBoost and graph-neural-network models to screen 11,576 DrugBank compounds. Researchers selected 15 candidates for evaluation; four met the study’s activity cutoff against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv. Aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin were further tested against multidrug-resistant isolates, intracellular bacteria and recombinant DNA gyrase. These are laboratory repurposing results, not evidence of patient benefit or clinical safety. A same-team patent-family publication predates the journal article; this record makes no priority claim over patent disclosures. Concentration values are omitted because of inconsistent units in the rendered tables.

Technology: Ensemble virtual screening with XGBoost and graph neural networks

Editorial relevance 60 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Multiple learned models, including XGBoost and graph neural networks, predicted antitubercular activity in a DrugBank screen and contributed to selection of candidates for experimental evaluation.
Test and result
The article reports follow-up testing of 15 selected compounds, four meeting the authors’ activity cutoff against H37Rv, and additional assays of aldoxorubicin and quarfloxin against multidrug-resistant isolates and recombinant DNA gyrase.
Limitation / still unknown
All reported results are in vitro. The study does not establish patient efficacy, clinical safety or the compounds’ cellular mechanism. Precise concentration values are omitted because table units are inconsistent; an earlier patent-family publication is noted without a priority claim.

28 Dec 2024Doctoral School of Medicine, "Victor Babes" University of Medicine and Pharmacy, 300041 Timisoara, Romania

Diabetes and Cataracts Development-Characteristics, Subtypes and Predictive Modeling Using Machine Learning in Romanian Patients: A Cross-Sectional Study.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Full MDPI text reviewed in Chrome: a cross-sectional study of 201 cataract patients (105 with diabetes) applies Random Forest classification to cataract subtype combinations. Cortical cataract was significantly more frequent in diabetes (p<0.0001); diabetes status, duration and diabetic polyneuropathy were important classification features. Approve narrowly as an exploratory cohort-specific association/classification result, not longitudinal prediction of cataract development. The reviewed source supports this bounded result; external generalization, causal effects, and sustained operational impact remain unestablished where the source reports retrospective or internal evaluation.

Technology: Random Forest classification predicts one-, two- or three-subtype cataract associations from patient factors; model is applied to a cross-sectional cohort.

PlantRNA-FM identifies translation-associated RNA motifs and structure motifs in plants

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The PlantRNA-FM model, pretrained on sequence and predicted RNA structure from 1,124 plant transcriptomes, identified 5′-UTR motifs associated with translation efficiency across plant transcriptomes. Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold. The paper reports the rG4 motifs as translation-repressive, consistent with prior evidence on individual rG4s; the transcriptome-wide model prioritization and tested instances are the scoped findings here.

Technology: PlantRNA-FM, an interpretable RNA foundation model integrating RNA sequence and predicted structure

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PlantRNA-FM was pretrained with plant RNA sequence and structure data, then fine-tuned on translation-efficiency data. An attention-contrast interpretation framework prioritized 5′-UTR sequence/structure motifs associated with translation; researchers tested selected motif predictions by mutating reporter constructs and measuring translation efficiency in plants.
Test and result
Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold.
Limitation / still unknown
Experimental reporter validation was limited to selected motifs and had n=3, as reported in the figure caption. The model’s transcriptome-wide associations are not individually causal validations. The repressive role of rG4 motifs was previously known for individual cases; the paper’s contribution includes model-prioritized plant 5′-UTR motifs and experimental effects for selected constructs, not first discovery of rG4 biology. Reporter assays do not establish whole-plant phenotype or crop benefit.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Spatial N-glycan imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissue and paired serum identified thirteen altered glycan structures; glycoproteomics linked them to more than 50 proteins, and sixteen glycoproteins were assessed in a separate patient set. Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.

Technology: Machine-learning algorithms using serum N-glycan and glycoprotein features, age, sex and AFP

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Researchers used spatial glycan imaging and glycoproteomics to select altered tissue and matched-serum features, then used machine-learning algorithms to combine selected glycan/glycoprotein measurements with clinical variables for HCC-versus-cirrhosis classification. The source reports model performance in an independent case-control patient set.
Test and result
Machine-learning algorithms combining glycan/glycoprotein features with clinical variables differentiated early-stage HCC from cirrhosis in a case-control cohort of 100 HCC and 101 cirrhosis-only patients, with reported AUROC values across the algorithms of 0.88–0.97.
Limitation / still unknown
The discovery samples included 53 HCC tissues and 23 matched sera; the 201-patient testing set was a case-control cohort, not prospective surveillance. Individual glycoforms were weak classifiers; performance came from combined feature algorithms.

2 Nov 2024Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; collaborating institutions

HiDDEN finds malignant-like cell signals in early multiple-myeloma precursor samples

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: HiDDEN refines sample-level case labels at single-cell resolution. In human bone-marrow single-cell RNA-seq data, its labels tracked manual neoplastic-cell annotations in mixed precursor samples and inferred malignant-like cells in three low-purity MGUS samples that the original manual analysis had labeled as containing only healthy cells. The inferred cells were enriched for previously described malignancy-associated gene signatures. In a separate mouse demyelination dataset, HiDDEN identified an early endothelial subpopulation with expression changes associated with angiogenesis, blood–brain-barrier breakdown and extracellular-matrix responses.

Technology: HiDDEN, a machine-learning framework for refining disease/condition labels at single-cell resolution

Editorial relevance 47 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model inferred which individual cells in case samples were affected rather than assigning the sample-level case label to all cells. This enabled the paper’s reanalysis of human myeloma precursor single-cell data and mouse demyelination single-nucleus data, yielding the specified malignancy and endothelial-population findings.
Test and result
HiDDEN refines sample-level case labels at single-cell resolution.
Limitation / still unknown
The MGUS finding is a transcriptomic inference in previously collected samples, computationally supported by known gene signatures and sample-purity estimates; the paper does not report independent pathology confirmation, clinical follow-up, or validation as a diagnostic test. The endothelial subpopulation was found in a mouse lesion model; its association with blood–brain-barrier dysfunction does not establish causality.

PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: PatternBoost alternates a local search that generates candidate constructions with a transformer trained on the best ones. The authors report the best known solutions to several extremal combinatorics problems, including a counterexample to a conjecture that had been open for 30 years. 31 Oct 2024Tri-Service General Hospital; National Defense Medical Center

Abdominal-X-ray network classifies recorded colorectal-cancer status

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A DenseNet-121 analyzed abdominal X-rays against recorded colorectal-cancer labels in Taiwanese hospital data. It achieved AUC 0.738 in 16,875 internal-validation patients and 0.656 in 15,876 patients from a community hospital; external sensitivity was 47.7% at the selected cutoff. Cancer was uncommon, registry records could miss diagnoses elsewhere, and the one-year follow-up/label timing limits claims about detection at the image date. This retrospective study does not establish effective screening or earlier diagnosis.

Technology: DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A 121-layer DenseNet learns radiographic patterns associated with recorded colorectal-cancer labels and returns a case probability for a single abdominal radiograph.
Test and result
Patient-separated development, tuning and validation cohorts, one randomly selected KUB radiograph per person, and registry/EMR colorectal-cancer labels. The threshold chosen in the tuning set was reused in both validation cohorts; external AUC .656 and sensitivity 47.7% were lower than internal results.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective screening performance, time gained before diagnosis and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Prior cancer was excluded and one-year follow-up used, but the precise diagnosis-to-image timing is not fully specified. Low case prevalence, distal-tumor imbalance and incomplete capture of outside-hospital diagnoses limit interpretation.

Technology: Neural curve classifier; weekly logistic aggregation

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A trained two-layer neural classifier maps acceleration/deceleration heart-rate curves to disease labels; learned weekly aggregation and contrastive training enable the represented clinical-label test.
Test and result
The ME-TIME cohort contained 42 participants. Thirty were used for development and subject-separated tuning; the test comprised six reference participants and six with atrial fibrillation or heart failure. Sensitivity/specificity average per-person weekly scores, not independent weekly patients.
Limitation / still unknown
Reference and disease groups differ in age, BMI and comorbidity. Twelve test participants and correlated weeks limit precision and generalization. Variant comparisons are exploratory. Several discussion paragraphs conflict with Table3 or misinterpret high specificity as a rule-out guarantee; neither rule-out safety nor prevention benefit is represented. Prospective data collection does not establish a frozen prospective model evaluation.

Technology: LASSO; sparse partial least-squares discriminant analysis

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Penalized model fitting selects and combines expression features linked to subsequent clinical status; the learned signature, not conventional differential expression alone, supplies the scoped finding.
Test and result
The prospective source cohort enrolled 720 newborns; day-of-birth expression comparisons included 14 later early-onset cases, six late-onset cases, 12 localized-infection cases and 32 healthy controls. Repeated development splits selected features; the final four-gene model used all available birth samples. The separate GSE26440 check comprised six early-onset cases and six controls.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective sample collection does not establish that the fitted model was frozen before outcomes. The headline development AUC .94 is not a held-out future-patient estimate; Monte Carlo testing and final whole-cohort fitting are distinct analyses. External post-onset samples do not test prediction before clinical symptoms. Tiny case counts, clinical sepsis definitions and selected controls limit generalization. No prevention or causal immune-development mechanism is represented.

24 Oct 2024German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ); Met Office; University of New South Wales; Freie Universität Berlin

AI reconstruction extends the 1911 French heatwave signal into September

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A partial-convolution U-Net trained on CMIP6 climate simulations and transferred to European station-based extreme indices reconstructed the poorly observed 1911 heatwave. The model estimates that in parts of southern France, more than 40% of September days exceeded the 90th percentile of maximum temperature, extending the heatwave signal into fall. The reconstructed pattern is similar to 20th Century Reanalysis Version 3 and aligns spatially with higher French mortality in 1911; the HadEX3 gridded record does not show the same pronounced heat.

Technology: Climate Reconstruction AI (CRAI), a U-Net with partial convolutions trained on CMIP6 historical simulations and transferred to the HadEX-CAM European extreme-index dataset

Editorial relevance 47 climate Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The deep-learning reconstruction inferred missing monthly temperature-extreme indices from spatial context and learned climate-model patterns. This enabled a detailed estimate for the poorly observed September 1911 period; the model output exposes hot extremes in southern France that are not clearly represented in the standard HadEX3 map and supports comparison with independent 20th Century Reanalysis and historical mortality patterns.
Test and result
A partial-convolution U-Net trained on CMIP6 climate simulations and transferred to European station-based extreme indices reconstructed the poorly observed 1911 heatwave.
Limitation / still unknown
The September 1911 values are AI reconstructions rather than newly recovered thermometer readings; the paper states the source observations are sparse or missing. CRAI is trained on CMIP6 simulations and applied to European station-based extreme-index fields, so model-prior dependence remains. The article reports a similar spatial pattern in 20CRv3 and correlation with 1911 mortality, but these support the reconstructed pattern rather than directly validate each missing grid cell. The reported >40% refers to predicted percentage of days above the local 90th percentile for maximum temperature.

23 Oct 2024Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; The Jackson Laboratory; Yale University

Machine-guided synthetic regulatory DNA drives cell-type-specific expression across cell lines and vertebrates

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The CODA platform used the Malinois deep-learning model and sequence-search algorithms to design synthetic cis-regulatory elements (CREs). In massively parallel reporter assays, 94.1% of the synthetic sequences met the authors’ cell-type-specificity criterion, versus 73.6% of model-selected natural sequences and 40.6% of chromatin-mark-selected natural sequences; synthetic sequences also had higher measured target/off-target separation across K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells. In transgenic zebrafish, two of three liver-directed and two of three neuron-directed CREs showed the intended activity. One neuron-directed sequence, synN1, retained cortical and neuronal expression in mice, including postnatal neocortical layer 6 and subplate neurons.

Technology: CODA (Computational Optimization of DNA Activity) with Malinois deep neural network and AdaLead, simulated annealing, and Fast SeqProp sequence search/design algorithms

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Malinois predicted MPRA activity of candidate DNA sequences in K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells; CODA iteratively optimized sequences for specified cell-type specificity. Researchers synthesized and experimentally measured the designs by MPRA, then tested selected CREs with reporter constructs in zebrafish and mice. The paper attributes the novel sequences and their measured expression specificity to this model-guided design loop.
Test and result
In massively parallel reporter assays, 94.1% of the synthetic sequences met the authors’ cell-type-specificity criterion, versus 73.6% of model-selected natural sequences and 40.6% of chromatin-mark-selected natural sequences; synthetic sequences also had higher measured target/off-target separation across K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells.
Limitation / still unknown
The in-vitro work used three transformed human cell lines and reporter assays. In-vivo testing covered a small selected set: two of three liver-directed and two of three neuron-directed elements were active in zebrafish; mouse validation focused on neuronal synN1, with n=3 synN1 mice for postnatal cell-type analysis and n=6 for the 5-week cortical reporter assay. These are transgenic reporter results, not therapeutic delivery or evidence of clinical utility. Earlier synthetic enhancer studies existed; this paper’s counted result is its CODA/Malinois comparison against natural sequences plus selected vertebrate validation, not the general idea of AI-designed enhancers.

11 Oct 2024Gladstone-UCSF Institute of Genomic Immunology; University of California, San Francisco; Johns Hopkins University; Stanford University; University of California, Berkeley

CRISPR perturbation and Bayesian network inference map immune-disease regulatory cascades in primary CD4+ T cells

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections. Integrating the inferred network with immune GWAS analyses identified an interconnected module in which KMT2A was inferred upstream of JAK-STAT and IL-2 signaling regulators including IRF4, STAT5A/B and IL2RA, linking an epigenetic regulator to immune-disease-associated pathways.

Technology: Linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB), a Bayesian extension of linear latent causal network inference, applied to CRISPR knockout and RNA-sequencing data

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
LLCB inferred direct and indirect regulatory relationships from perturbation-associated expression effects across 84 targeted genes. The model-derived network and gene-program analysis, combined with immune GWAS statistics, supported the specific KMT2A-to-JAK-STAT/IL-2 regulatory finding. CRISPR perturbation supplied the experimental perturbation data; the network algorithm converted those measurements into the reported regulatory map.
Test and result
The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections.
Limitation / still unknown
The study perturbed 84 selected genes in primary CD4+ T cells from three donors, so this is not a complete T-cell regulatory map. LLCB “direct effects” are statistical effects adjusted for other perturbed genes and are not evidence of physical binding; effects from unperturbed genes can be attributed to modeled edges. The GWAS integration identifies pathway links, not proof that the inferred cascade causes clinical disease. A prior bioRxiv version (10.1101/2023.09.17.557749) is the same study and is not counted separately.

4 Oct 2024University of Wisconsin-Madison

Iterative Gaussian process screening discovers selective aurein-derived antifungal peptides

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An uncertainty-aware Gaussian process regression workflow iteratively selected 23 synthetic α/β-peptide analogues for synthesis and measurements of fungal inhibition and human-red-blood-cell hemolysis. One lead, peptide 6-4, was a measured variant of an existing aurein-derived template and achieved a selectivity index of 57.1 (60.9 using the study’s finer MIC interval) versus 1.2 for aurein 1.2. Its high selectivity was driven by low hemolysis; the result is a specific peptide-design and assay contribution, not a new peptide scaffold or evidence of therapeutic efficacy. The ChemRxiv v1 result was posted on 2024-10-04; the peer-reviewed journal article followed in 2025.

The model estimated the measurement-noise level from noisy experimental data, incorporated that level into Kriging predictions, and used a noise-augmented acquisition strategy to choose the next NiTi-based compositions. 29 Sep 2024Soochow University; Xuzhou Medical University; Nantong University; Nanjing Medical University

Learned mutation score associates with survival in checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An XGBoost mutation score separated observed survival groups in public cohorts of checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer. The source used 123 patients for initial fitting and two additional cohort groups of 42 and 66 for model comparison. Because those comparison cohorts helped select the final model, the result is an exploratory prognostic association rather than untouched external validation or evidence of treatment benefit.

Technology: XGBoost mutation-feature selection and boosted survival-risk modeling

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned feature-selection and boosted model combined tumor mutation profiles into the represented survival-associated score; immune enrichment analyses alone are not the admission basis.
Test and result
The paper defined overall survival in checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer as the endpoint. A 123-person MSK cohort supplied initial prognostic-gene filtering. It compared 297 algorithm combinations using cohort groups of 42 and 66 and selected the highest mean test-cohort concordance. The selected XGBoost procedure retained twelve mutation features, with a training-derived median score threshold separating survival groups across the represented cohorts.
Limitation / still unknown
The purported validation cohorts were used for final model selection and therefore do not establish an untouched external test. Participant overlap between public source cohorts was not independently reconstructed. Small cohort groups, extensive model searching and differing sequencing panels increase optimism and transportability concerns. Survival among treated patients does not identify benefit relative to no treatment or distinguish predictive treatment-response effects from general prognosis. Drug-sensitivity predictions and cell-line experiments are outside this admitted case, and no therapeutic efficacy is claimed.

Technology: Multilayer perceptron behavior classification from accelerometer and gyroscope features

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The trained multilayer classifier converted sensor streams into behavior labels; conventional temporal counting/statistical comparisons then quantified the source-specific housing contrast.
Test and result
A two-hen labeled training/evaluation step supplied separate housing-specific classifiers. A later recording step used five hens in both housing systems, averaging 4.5 recording days per bird/housing condition. Those later recordings were not reused training data. The source reports more detected transitions involving moving, preening, dust-bathing, litter scratching, resting, tail-wagging and body shaking in floor pens. Visual-scan comparison in a sampled floor-pen video gave correlation .94.
Limitation / still unknown
There were only five birds in the housing comparison; repeated days/intervals are not independent birds. Basic same-bird classification accuracy differed substantially by housing (77.5% cages, 96.3% floor pens), and overlapping sensor windows may affect internal validation. The source does not establish that differential errors cannot explain part of the transition contrast. Training-bird overlap with the later five-bird population is not excluded, although recording data were separate. Pooling days and thresholding transitions do not establish a population-general causal welfare measure. Spatial location came from a colored marker rather than a learned tracking model.

A conditional variational autoencoder generated candidate alloy compositions and an artificial neural network ranked eutectic-forming likelihood.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Test and result
The source retained 1,288 people from J-ACCESS 3/4 and analyzed stress/rest volumes separately. Expert 17-segment perfusion grades trained a U-Net/CNN scorer. Exchanging validation and test roles compromises an untouched-test interpretation. Ninety-six percent of source segments were normal or mildly abnormal, so aggregate agreement does not establish sensitivity for severe disease. Expert interpretation is the reference, not invasive disease truth or measured subsequent prognosis. The test is small and no clinical benefit was demonstrated.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned view classifiers select inferior-vena-cava inspiration videos; a trained SlowFast R50 model assigns three pressure categories from their static and temporal features.
Test and result
15,828 archived studies from 11,869 patients were divided by patient into 12,664 training, 1,582 validation and 1,582 test studies. The full test AUROC was 0.823; the abstract's 0.844 refers to a quality-filtered 554-study subset. External evaluation retained 2,618 Montreal studies and yielded weighted AUROC 0.854 against cardiologist categories. All 319 catheter-paired studies were kept in testing; model accuracy against binned catheter values was 49.5%, versus 48.9% for cardiologist estimates.
Limitation / still unknown
Catheter and ultrasound measurements could be up to 30 days apart. A nonsignificant difference is not an equivalence test. External reference labels were cardiologist estimates rather than catheter measurements, and external image-quality filtering excludes many original studies. Weighted metrics use UCSF class frequencies. Automated scan selection can pick a different video from the one used clinically. No prospective workflow benefit, prevention effect or safe replacement of invasive measurement is established.

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

AI contribution
The fitted ensemble classified spatial fluorescence-feature samples using the surgeon’s labels, enabling an explicit held-video reference-agreement test.
Test and result
Seven training videos supplied 28 sampled lines and 1,413 image grids; three test videos supplied three lines and 149 grids. Testing agreed on 138 of 138 reference retain labels and 10 of 11 reference excise labels, giving 99.3% overall grid accuracy.
Limitation / still unknown
All ten patients were selected for absence of later partial or total flap necrosis. The reference was one experienced surgeon’s original decisions, not an independent tissue-viability endpoint. Many adjacent grids came from only three held-out patients; internal ten-fold grid validation is not independent-patient validation. Prospective recording of videos does not establish prospective deployment or clinical benefit of the learned model.

The authors then tested LPA in infection models, including cultured porcine alveolar macrophages and infected pigs, to examine host-response and disease outcomes.
Test and result
Machine-learning analysis of untargeted serum metabolomic and lipidomic profiles from clinical pig cohorts identified lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) as a PRRSV-associated biomarker.
Limitation / still unknown
The clinical classifier and biomarker work concerns pigs, not human diagnosis. The infection challenge experiments were small (figure descriptions report five piglets per group), and cell assays were performed in vitro. The authors report that the mechanism by which LPA suppresses RIG-I remains unclear; the findings do not establish a treatment for people or broad field effectiveness in livestock.

AI contribution

The patient validation was a small case-control pilot (30 first-episode cases and 30 healthy controls); its AUC of 0.755 is modest and has a wide confidence interval. CENPI methylation did not differ in the clinical samples, so it should not be presented as independently validated. The study does not establish diagnostic performance in clinical differential-diagnosis populations, prospective utility or causality, and the authors describe the signature as potentially useful for future diagnostics rather than clinically established.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

AI contribution

A semi-supervised PhaseNet-TF workflow detected and relocated 13,616 events from a one-year Tonga OBS and land-station record, about 11 times the manually picked reference catalog.
Limitation / still unknown
The catalog is based on one year of OBS and land data. About half of events are outside the array and have larger hypocenter uncertainty from azimuthal gaps; velocity-model choice adds absolute-location uncertainty. The authors say the absent 350–460 km double zone may reflect insufficient events, not definitive absence. Stress and hydration explanations are interpretations, and some rare events above the slab may be false.

30 May 2024Yale School of Medicine; Biohaven Pharmaceuticals; Massachusetts General Hospital; UCLA School of Medicine

Post hoc neural gait analysis detects a tandem-walk metric difference in an ataxia trial

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A deep pose-estimation pipeline extracted gait measurements from a small convenience subset of a randomized ataxia trial. Post hoc analysis found a tandem-walk metric difference between troriluzole and placebo, while the natural-walk comparison was nonsignificant and treatment did not reduce falls. The result supports a bounded retrospective measurement finding, without confirmatory evidence of clinical benefit.

Technology: MPII-trained multi-stage deep neural network for human pose estimation; derived Pose Dispersion Index

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned pose model extracted body coordinates from trial videos, enabling a source-specific gait metric and treatment-group comparison that standard clinician ratings did not directly provide. Trial randomization does not make this later AI-derived endpoint a locked prospective evaluation.
Test and result
Among 218 randomized participants, interpretable paired videos were available for 67 tandem-walk and 56 natural-walk participants. The pretrained deep network tracked body keypoints used to calculate pose dispersion. An adjusted treatment-by-visit mixed model reported a week 48 tandem-walk coefficient 0.584, 95% CI 0.137–1.031, p=0.010. The natural-walk difference was nonsignificant, and the source explicitly reports no treatment effect on falls.
Limitation / still unknown
The video endpoint was post hoc and was not the original recording purpose. Convenience and quality selection retained only 30.7% and 25.7% of participants, respectively, introducing selection and measurement limitations. Only baseline/final recordings were analyzed, supplementary metric implementation was not independently reconstructed, and the finding does not establish prespecified efficacy, reduced falls or clinical utility.

29 May 2024Department of General Surgery, General Hospital of Northern Theater Command, Shenyang, China

Machine-learning analysis linked two sepsis-associated neutrophil clusters to five mouse-validated marker genes

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Reanalysis of single-cell profiles from four sepsis patients and two healthy controls identified two neutrophil clusters enriched in the sepsis samples and a set of cluster-associated gene modules. LASSO and seven additional machine-learning classifiers prioritized eight hub genes, including ALPL, CD177, S100A8, S100A9 and STXBP2. Expression analyses in separate public sepsis transcriptome cohorts supported several markers, and qRT-PCR in cecal-ligation/puncture and LPS mouse models found increased neutrophil expression of those five genes. The result links sepsis-associated neutrophil states to a small marker panel, with experimental expression validation in mice.

Technology: LASSO feature selection followed by seven machine-learning classifiers (k-nearest neighbors, linear discriminant analysis, logistic regression, naive Bayes, random forest, recursive partitioning and support-vector machine), combined with hdWGCNA and single-cell transcriptomic analysis

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Machine-learning feature selection prioritized eight hub genes from expression modules associated with the two sepsis-enriched neutrophil clusters. The models were assessed on separate public training and validation transcriptome cohorts; the resulting marker set guided qRT-PCR validation of five genes in two sepsis mouse models.
Test and result
Expression analyses in separate public sepsis transcriptome cohorts supported several markers, and qRT-PCR in cecal-ligation/puncture and LPS mouse models found increased neutrophil expression of those five genes.
Limitation / still unknown
The single-cell discovery comparison was very small (four sepsis cases and two controls) and the two clusters are analysis-derived states in this dataset; the study does not establish that they are distinct universal neutrophil lineages. The public bulk cohorts validate expression/classification associations, not an independent single-cell subtype. qRT-PCR confirmed expression changes for five genes in mouse models; it did not test whether the genes cause sepsis phenotypes or are therapeutic targets. The article itself notes earlier reports of other sepsis-related neutrophil subtypes, so this record is bounded to its specific clusters/markers and assays.

Test and result
StarDist was trained on manually annotated human and mouse pancreatic-cancer-organoid images. Learned segmentation enabled image-derived counts, area and size-group trajectories during experimental treatment. AI contribution
GPT-3.5 was queried about fly gene functions and used to construct hypothesized relationships among behavioral-screen candidates; it proposed a MRE11–Dop1R1 link that researchers tested pharmacologically. Test and result
The source split 634 prostatectomy patients into 507 development and 127 test patients. Fixed segmentation models produced prostate/lesion masks; geometric features trained random forests with repeated cross-validation. Limitation / still unknown
This retrospective analysis used prospectively recorded radiologist assessments, without prospective AI-model locking. Development grades partly incorporated pathology, while comparison grades came from the radiologist. Reused segmentation models and overlapping institutional recruitment periods mean the full pipeline is not established as wholly unfamiliar with test patients. No paired clinical reader-assistance or treatment-benefit trial was performed, and no general superiority is claimed.

AI contribution
The random-forest surrogates estimated unperturbed cloud properties and radiative fluxes for given meteorological conditions. Comparing those counterfactuals with observations in four volcanic plume episodes isolated aerosol-associated signals from meteorological co-variability and enabled estimates of cloud-cover, rainfall, and radiative-forcing responses across distinct tropical meteorological regimes.

Using satellite observations of four Kīlauea volcanic outgassing episodes in 2008 and 2018, an ML counterfactual analysis found that volcanic aerosols increased cloud cover and reflected sunlight over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, even as rainfall strengthened.

This is an observational ML-counterfactual analysis of four Kīlauea plume months over tropical marine shallow-convective clouds, not a controlled aerosol intervention or a direct test of deliberate cloud seeding. The source reports strong cloud-cover responses and radiative estimates, especially under humid/stable conditions, but results depend on satellite retrievals and the learned unperturbed baseline. The authors’ proposed mechanism for increased cloud cover alongside stronger rainfall is explicitly a hypothesis requiring further testing; do not treat the marine-cloud-brightening scenario as experimentally demonstrated.

28 Mar 2024Singapore Eye Research Institute; Singapore National Eye Centre; National University of Singapore; Duke-NUS Medical School

Machine learning links circulating tyrosine and distinct lipid-metabolite features to diabetic kidney disease and retinopathy detection

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In 2,772 adults with diabetes from Singapore’s population-based SEED study, LASSO and gradient-boosting models screened 220 circulating metabolites and 19 clinical factors for prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and retinopathy (DR), then were externally assessed in 5,843 UK Biobank participants. Both outcomes shared diabetes duration, insulin use, age and tyrosine as important model features. DKD additionally selected cardiovascular disease history, antihypertensive use, lactate, citrate and the intermediate-density-lipoprotein cholesterol-ester/total-lipid ratio; DR additionally selected HbA1c, glucose, pulse pressure and alanine. External AUCs were 0.791 for DKD and 0.778 for DR, versus 0.691 and 0.760 for conventional adjusted logistic-regression comparators.

Technology: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression and gradient-boosting decision trees applied to metabolomics and clinical risk factors

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
ML feature selection prioritized a shared set of clinical/metabolic factors and distinct DKD- and DR-associated metabolites, then built detection models externally evaluated in UK Biobank. These models outperformed traditional adjusted logistic-regression comparators in the reported internal and external validation. The scientific result is the disease-specific feature pattern and its validated detection performance, not merely an algorithm benchmark.
Test and result
In 2,772 adults with diabetes from Singapore’s population-based SEED study, LASSO and gradient-boosting models screened 220 circulating metabolites and 19 clinical factors for prevalent diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and retinopathy (DR), then were externally assessed in 5,843 UK Biobank participants.
Limitation / still unknown
The analysis is retrospective and cross-sectional; it classifies prevalent complications and cannot establish temporal prediction or causal effects of tyrosine, lactate, citrate, alanine or lipid features. The Singapore cohort was recruited in 2004–2011 and was multiethnic Asian; about 95% had type 2 diabetes, but the study did not separate diabetes types. UK Biobank definitions and available eye-severity measures differed, and validation of moderate-or-worse DR was not feasible. Performance is modest, particularly external AUC 0.791 DKD/0.778 DR, and does not establish clinical utility.

EHR machine learning and genetic colocalization link osteoporosis to female Alzheimer’s risk near MS4A6A

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Random-forest models trained on UCSF records (749 expert-diagnosed Alzheimer’s disease cases and 250,545 controls) identified clinical features predictive up to seven years before the recorded onset; the seven-year model’s AUROC was 0.72 using clinical features alone. Matched-cohort follow-up in external University of California health-system records found faster Alzheimer’s diagnosis after osteoporosis in women. Genetic colocalization analyses supported a female-specific shared signal between Alzheimer’s disease, low heel bone mineral density and MS4A6A expression near the MS4A gene cluster. The paper also reports shared APOE-locus support for hyperlipidemia and Alzheimer’s disease.

Technology: Random-forest models on longitudinal electronic health records, interpreted with the SPOKE biomedical knowledge network

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Random-forest models ranked EHR-derived clinical features associated with future Alzheimer’s diagnosis. The team used matched models to prioritize hypotheses, then used SPOKE to connect clinical predictors to biological networks and independent health-system data plus GWAS/eQTL colocalization to examine the osteoporosis and hyperlipidemia associations. The model-generated prioritization led to follow-up of the female-specific osteoporosis signal near MS4A6A.
Test and result
Matched-cohort follow-up in external University of California health-system records found faster Alzheimer’s diagnosis after osteoporosis in women.
Limitation / still unknown
This is hypothesis-generating observational work. EHR features may reflect healthcare access, clinician behavior, coding and biological processes; the authors explicitly state that further validation across omics data types is needed. Genetic colocalization and matched cohort associations do not establish that osteoporosis causes Alzheimer’s disease or that treating osteoporosis prevents it. The prediction model is not a prospective clinical-impact evaluation, and early risk discrimination is modest with the low-prevalence outcome.

The team compared regression with classification methods across cohorts, externally validated HRD predictions in CPTAC, and tested prognostic associations of predicted scores in a separate retrospective colorectal-cancer cohort.
Test and result
On TCGA internal validation, HRD classification AUROC exceeded 0.70 in five of seven cancer types; external CPTAC validation reached AUROC 0.81 for lung adenocarcinoma and 0.96 for endometrial cancer.
Limitation / still unknown
Retrospective computational pathology analysis; the model predicts molecular and immune-related biomarkers from slides and does not replace confirmatory molecular testing or establish treatment selection benefit. HRD performance varied by cancer type, with weak internal performance in some cohorts. The reported survival associations in DACHS are prognostic associations, not evidence that using model predictions improves patient outcomes. Scores and endpoints were tested in the named datasets.

AI contribution
A previously developed learned segmenter provides manually checked epicardial-fat masks; selected handcrafted spatial/intensity features enter a fitted regularized survival model. AI credit concerns measurement and model fitting, not a new fat-inflammation mechanism.
Test and result
The original v1 Methods and Results use 400 archived CT records, with 56% event prevalence and a random 320/80 development/test split. Feature selection is described as training-only. The v1 reports the same 0.69 test C-index as the later journal version.

In a proteomic study, researchers measured paired CSF and serum samples in a discovery cohort and used random-forest machine learning to select a 19-protein CSF panel and an eight-protein serum panel to distinguish mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer disease from cognitively normal participants.
Limitation / still unknown
The AUC test sets were small (CSF: 9 Alzheimer-related MCI and 21 controls; serum: 8 and 21). The study used separate independent multicenter targeted-proteomics validation for candidate proteins; that does not make the small classifier test cohorts large or establish clinical utility. The serum panel was less effective at distinguishing Alzheimer-related MCI from other neurodegenerative diseases than the CSF panel. These are research panels, not routine tests.

Active learning identifies experimentally improved ammonia catalysts

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Literature-trained models and iterative experimental feedback guided a predetermined ammonia-catalyst search. Selected formulations exceeded many reported comparator activities in the authors' laboratory measurements. Initial literature-only predictions were insufficient, making feedback essential. This is a bounded formulation result, not demonstrated commercial green-ammonia performance or invention of promoted ruthenium catalysis.

2 Jan 2024Southeast University

Machine learning-guided synthesis of two-dimensional AgBi iodide perovskites

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The authors combined an 80-amine high-throughput synthesis dataset, chemistry-informed molecular descriptors, subgroup discovery and a support-vector classifier to rank organic spacers for 2D AgBi iodide perovskites. Of 13 model-selected candidates taken forward, eight were successfully synthesized and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction. The study reports a 61.5% success rate in this selected validation set; it does not establish universal synthesis performance across other perovskite families.

Technology: Subgroup discovery and support-vector classification using physicochemical and molecular-topology descriptors

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Subgroup discovery identifies an applicable data region and a support-vector classifier estimates synthesis feasibility from molecular descriptors; the model ranks candidate organic spacers for experimental synthesis.
Test and result
The primary article reports successful synthesis of 8 of 13 machine-learning-selected 2D AgBi iodide perovskites (61.5%), with crystal structures determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and bulk-phase purity confirmed by PXRD.
Limitation / still unknown
The validation concerns a selected set under common laboratory synthesis conditions and one AgBi iodide family; generalization to other material families is not demonstrated.
